notes: Stance: all four documents agreed (three delegates, iSchool permit). Units were matched by source passage. Coders differed in granularity: B merged the CFETI Turnitin-limits consultation with the Turnitin Clarity workshop, split the faculty 'must report' duty from the 'no sanction without the form' rule, and gave the Turnitin access sentence its own unit; A split the AI-statement sentences in the library guide and coded a rationale for reporting and the forthcoming-training announcement. Only-one-coder units were checked against the text; 5 only_A and 4 of 6 only_B were kept as real statements. B's two generic iSchool plagiarism-procedure units (report to Student Conduct, sanction options) were dropped because the passages never mention AI. Main disagreements: (1) actor: admin vs instructor/student for resources offered (CFETI consultations, AI Literacy course, Career Center), resolved to the addressee of the text (instructor or student), and all for the general fairness and adoption-date statements; (2) modality: must vs must-not for the sanction-needs-form rule, resolved to must-not by 'may not be imposed'; must vs should for the iSchool 'responsibility to confer', resolved to must; informs vs may for the tutoring pointer, resolved to informs; both coders had should for the detector 'must ... be approached with great caution', changed to must following the source verb; (3) policy_type: P40 vs P92 for 'Faculty may only use detection services approved by the university', resolved to P92 with a fit_note; (4) phase: Writing Center tutoring pointer, resolved to general. unit_stance disagreements (permit vs require for the iSchool citation duty, restrict vs neutral for the detector sole-basis rule) were also resolved from the text.
